Walk it

Steps

Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory Reporting➔Inventory Position➔Company - Item Inventory (whwmd4100m100)

Why LN works this way. When the command is chosen, LN runs the dataset for the record on the screen, writes the result into the prompt text and sends it to the model. The answer opens in a window of its own. The dataset gives the model its LN facts, but the answer can still add things that aren't in them, such as totals of its own. A wrong answer looks the same as a right one, so check the first answer against the screen, then read it for anything nobody asked for.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Close any open tab of your screen
5.2Open your screen and tick a record whose answer you can check. Example: an item with stock in two warehouses
5.3Note the values the answer should state. Example: the item's on hand and on order figures on its rowWrite downexpected values
5.4Open Actions and choose your commandA window with your sentence under Prompt and the answer under Response
5.5Compare the answer with your expected valuesThe facts should match. Example: the warehouses' figures add up to the row's
5.6Read the answer for what the prompt text did not ask forExample: a report with a column of the model's own sums, one of them wrong, and a promise

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
The command isn't in ActionsRead the session code in the status bar of the screen and compare it with step 4.2 (Link the prompt to a session), character for character. On a tab of a workbench the status bar shows the workbench; read the tab's code in its own Personalize Form, as in step 1.3 (Plan the prompt)
The command is still missing and the code is rightCheck that Active is ticked on the link, then close the screen's tab and open it again
The command is in Actions but greyed outThe link may be waiting for a ticked record. Tick one, or set When Enabled to Always, as in step 4.3 (Link the prompt to a session)
An error names dataset.get.selection.index and a tableThe dataset's main table isn't the screen's. The table in the message is the screen's: build the dataset on it, or link the prompt to a screen on your table

Set up a GenAI prompt
Run it and check the answer

  1. This task starts at Warehousing➔Inventory Reporting➔Inventory Position➔Company - Item Inventory (whwmd4100m100)

    Close any open tab of your screen

  2. Open your screen and tick a record whose answer you can check

    Example: an item with stock in two warehouses

  3. Note the values the answer should state

    Example: the item's on hand and on order figures on its row

    Write down

  4. Open Actions and choose your command

    You should see

    A window with your sentence under Prompt and the answer under Response

  5. Compare the answer with your expected values

    You should see

    The facts should match. Example: the warehouses' figures add up to the row's

  6. Read the answer for what the prompt text did not ask for

    You should see

    Example: a report with a column of the model's own sums, one of them wrong, and a promise

  • Kept in this browser until you start a new run.

    • The command isn't in Actions

      Read the session code in the status bar of the screen and compare it with step 2 of Link the prompt to a session, character for character. On a tab of a workbench the status bar shows the workbench; read the tab's code in its own Personalize Form, as in step 3 of Plan the prompt

    • The command is still missing and the code is right

      Check that Active is ticked on the link, then close the screen's tab and open it again

    • The command is in Actions but greyed out

      The link may be waiting for a ticked record. Tick one, or set When Enabled to Always, as in step 3 of Link the prompt to a session

    • An error names dataset.get.selection.index and a table

      The dataset's main table isn't the screen's. The table in the message is the screen's: build the dataset on it, or link the prompt to a screen on your table

  • When the command is chosen, LN runs the dataset for the record on the screen, writes the result into the prompt text and sends it to the model. The answer opens in a window of its own. The dataset gives the model its LN facts, but the answer can still add things that aren't in them, such as totals of its own. A wrong answer looks the same as a right one, so check the first answer against the screen, then read it for anything nobody asked for.
